instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Supportive Rage
cards.instruction: Remain helpful and encouraging while becoming increasingly furious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Blot the paint, don't scrub. Yes, like that. We can still save my sofa.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've stepped in it. There's paint on the carpet now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay exactly there. Good, you've stopped. I'll put newspaper under your feet before you redecorate my whole bloody house.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The newspaper's soaked through.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lift one foot. One, for God's sake. I'll slide my bath towel under it. You're doing fine; keep watching me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can change your birthday lunch. I'll handle the cancellation; we don't simply fail to turn up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want the seaside place, but we'd lose your forty-pound deposit here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Forty pounds down the drain. Fine, you deserve your sea view. Let me confirm a window table before you pay anyone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've paid another forty. They say a window table costs extra.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The supplement. An amount, please. Give me the phone; you're having your birthday by that bloody window.

cards.title: Terms and Conditions
cards.instruction: Treat every offer, favor, feeling, and apology as a negotiation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can borrow my ladder for two lifts to the station. Two separate journeys; we should define that now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only need the ladder for five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Duration affects the rate, not whether there is one. One lift, and you return it dry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll give you five pounds. We're friends; can we keep it simple?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Four pounds if you say we're good friends. Please specify that before I hand it over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll accept your apology for missing my birthday if you spend Boxing Day here. Arrival by noon; an evening visit isn't a day.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll come at noon. Will you tell Mum we're all right?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That is a separate request. Stay for dinner and I'll tell her there's no bad feeling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want there actually to be no bad feeling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then stay through New Year. Please don't ask for the full reconciliation at the reassuring-phone-call rate.

cards.title: Yes, but My Way
cards.instruction: Agree with others, then reinterpret the agreement entirely in your favor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll help move the sofa. First, stop pulling the arm; the weight needs to come from underneath.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. You take that end and I'll take this one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. I'll direct from that end. We need one person watching the doorway, not two people guessing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We need two people lifting. I'll get Sam, but you still have to help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. I'll correct both your grips before we start. Please don't make me supervise two different mistakes at once.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll look after your dog while the kitchen is repaired. Bring his usual food; sudden diet changes are poor practice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He needs to stay overnight. You'd have to give him breakfast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. Stay in my guest room and I'll show you the correct portion before bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed, I'll organise that. Walk before breakfast, please. Set your alarm for five thirty; I won't have him rushed because the handler overslept.

cards.title: The Pattern
cards.instruction: Treat every minor detail as evidence of a much larger problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two biscuits missing. Please don't refill the tin until I've established the weakness in our stock controls.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ate them. That's the mystery solved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The eater is not the weakness. Who issued you two biscuits without recording the withdrawal?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody. I was hungry and the tin was open.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Uncontrolled access and no meal provision. Two separate headings, please. List everyone who can reach that lid; I'll start the catering review.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody got my meeting email. Don't resend anything; first we identify the communication failure.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's in your drafts. You didn't send it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That is the immediate error, not the root cause. Why did nobody notice the office was waiting on one person?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send it while you have lunch. Problem solved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Temporary cover is not succession planning. Write down what else you'll take over while I eat; clearly we need to define your entire role.

cards.title: Could You Just…
cards.instruction: Turn a difficult task into tiny favors until the help quietly becomes most of the task.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you hold my shelf bracket for a moment? Against the pencil line, please. It needs to be level.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only a moment. I'm leaving for work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Just turn the top screw until it takes the weight. Gently; don't bury the head.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's holding. I've put the other screws in their holes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Just tighten those, then slide the shelf on to check the fit. Both hands, please. I'll fetch your coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you hold my bouquet stems together? Keep the flower heads level, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're level. You need wire under that ribbon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, a concealed binding. Could you twist this piece once, just below your fingers? Keep it tight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Done, but the end will catch on the dress.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tuck it inward, please. Just wind the ribbon over it and tie one small bow. Small, please; the bride is carrying flowers, not ribbon.
